source_name: Council of Europe MONEYVAL – evaluations hub and Montenegro mutual evaluation / follow-up reports
why_relevant: Fifth-round mutual evaluation of Montenegro (published Feb 2024, adopted Dec 2023) plus annual follow-up reports re-rating FATF recommendations. Directly assesses regulation and supervision of financial institutions, CDD, new technologies and virtual assets — the strongest external constraint on Montenegrin banks' and PSPs' compliance obligations.

source_name: FATF – Global Network page for MONEYVAL (and FATF statements affecting Montenegro)
why_relevant: Confirms the methodology and rating framework behind MONEYVAL findings and is the venue where grey-listing risk for Montenegro would materialise — a step change for correspondent banking and payments if it ever occurred.

source_name: ecoi.net – archived copies of EU and Council of Europe country documents on Montenegro
why_relevant: Independent mirror/archive of enlargement-package SWDs and related assessments with stable document IDs; useful fallback when Commission download links rotate, and a convenient way to enumerate document history.

source_name: Local media relay of supranational assessments (CdM, Standard, Mondo, Vijesti, ETV) — sr-language early signal
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets frequently publish draft EC report assessments and MONEYVAL outcomes days before official publication, and enumerate the specific measures/recommendations by chapter. Useful as a leading indicator and for local terminology, but must be corroborated against the primary document.

Specialist Montenegrin finance portal covering banks, capital markets, insurance and real estate. Publishes recurring analytical pieces built directly on CBCG and bank quarterly/annual reports (e.g. 'Analiza poslovanja banaka u Crnoj Gori', 'Banke za pola godine zaradile 63,9 miliona eura'), plus fee changes and appointments. Highest signal-per-article density in the cell.

Consistently the first outlet to publish aggregated bank-by-bank profit tables from CBCG quarterly data, well ahead of English coverage. Articles name individual banks (CKB, NLB, Hipotekarna, Razvojna banka) with euro figures, and cover CBCG financial-stability messaging.

source_name: Vijesti (ND Vijesti) — daily newspaper and portal, economy desk
why_relevant: Largest-circulation independent Montenegrin daily; its economy desk does investigative work on bank fees, CBCG supervision, ownership changes and licensing disputes, and frequently obtains documents ahead of official publication. Named explicitly in the cell definition.

source_name: Pobjeda — state-linked daily newspaper and portal
why_relevant: Oldest Montenegrin daily; carries government/CBCG-adjacent economic announcements, bank press releases and ministry statements. Useful as the establishment-side counterweight to Vijesti/Dan, and for official-channel signalling on payments policy (SEPA, fee regulation).

Confirmed live economy section with substantive banking/payments reporting: SEPA accession, external debt/IIP data from CBCG and Eurostat, Ministry of Finance hedging losses, and 'banks are the healthiest segment of the economy' analyses. Opposition-leaning framing surfaces complaints and disputes that do not appear in filings.

High-volume news portal that reliably republishes bank and CBCG press releases verbatim and quickly (bank anniversaries, CBCG blocked-accounts lists, CBCG award competitions, World Bank engagements). Excellent low-latency press-release feed for the Montenegrin banking sector.

source_name: RTCG — Radio Televizija Crne Gore, Ekonomija
why_relevant: National public broadcaster with a deep, permanently-archived economy section (article ids back to the early 2010s). Confirmed coverage of exactly the cell's target events: fee/commission increases by banks, bank capitalisations, new bank licences, Euromoney bank awards, household credit exposure. The archive depth makes it the best source for historical fee-change baselines.

National wire agency (founded 2002, Podgorica) with a dedicated business service covering Montenegroberza stock-exchange indices and bank fee/commission aggregates. Because most Montenegrin portals republish MINA copy, monitoring the wire identifies the original source of an item and gives earliest timestamps. Serves sr, Montenegrin, Albanian and English.

Regional (SRB-origin) business portal with a dedicated Montenegro edition covering bank interest and fee income, tenders, and Razvojna banka Crne Gore activity. Structured news ids and a tender/deal focus make it useful for deal-flow and vendor-opportunity signals alongside pure earnings.

Long-running independent weekly (since 1990) doing analytical/investigative economic journalism rather than daily reporting — bank guarantees, ownership networks, supervision failures. Lower volume but high interpretive value for understanding why a deal or appointment happened. Full PDF back-issues are posted on the site, giving unusual archive depth.

Online magazine founded 2014 in Podgorica focused on finance, business and — per its own positioning — the only fintech-oriented portal in Montenegro. Directly on-topic for the payments half of the sector brief (cards, digital wallets, PSP entrants) which the general dailies undercover.

News portal with a dedicated economy section and a browsable archive covering CBCG announcements (blocked-account lists), banking and regional economic news. The separate /arhiva/ekonomija path is valuable for structured historical backfill rather than only current headlines.

Active Montenegrin portal carrying Ministry of Finance and World Bank/IFI communications relevant to payments infrastructure — including the TIPS Clone integration and Montenegro's SEPA-zone positioning, i.e. exactly the infrastructure signals that precede vendor and bank procurement.

Secondary Montenegrin portal that carries named-official economic statements (e.g. minister/CBCG commentary on economic activity). Useful as a redundancy channel and for catching quotes that dailies trim, though it largely mirrors wire copy.

source_name: SEEbiz.eu — regional South-East European business portal
why_relevant: Regional business wire covering banks, funds, stock exchanges and macro across ex-Yugoslav markets in a mutually intelligible language. Valuable for cross-border parent-bank stories (NLB, Erste, OTP/CKB, Addiko) whose Montenegrin subsidiary implications are only reported regionally.

source_name: Biznis.rs — Serbian business portal, banking desk
why_relevant: Serbian-language banking desk with comparative consumer-cost coverage (ATM withdrawal fees abroad, card charges) that routinely spans Montenegro because of shared banking groups and the euro/dinar corridor. Complements domestic ME coverage on retail fee benchmarking.

Regional Bloomberg-licensed outlet publishing in the local language with Adria-region banking and macro coverage. Higher editorial standards than most regional portals and often the fastest local-language read on ECB/parent-group decisions that transmit to Montenegrin banks.

Not a news source but the authoritative registry of Montenegrin outlets with ownership structures and shareholding percentages (e.g. Monitor d.o.o. majority-held by the Perović family at 51.83%). Essential for scoring the credibility and political alignment of every other source in this cell, and for discovering outlets not surfaced by search.

source_name: Wikipedia — List of banks in Montenegro (actor-map pointer)
why_relevant: Fast actor-map scaffold enumerating licensed Montenegrin banks (CKB, NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna, Prva banka Crne Gore, Erste, Lovćen, Adriatic/First Financial, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Razvojna banka) with parent-group links. Use only to generate the search-term list; the authoritative register is CBCG's own bank list, and Wikipedia entries can be stale.

Local-language business directory listing Montenegrin banks with contact and site links. Low editorial value but useful as a snowball surface for local-language bank name spellings and for finding smaller institutions and MFIs missing from English lists.

source_name: Zavod za zapošljavanje Crne Gore (ZZZCG) — oglasi za slobodna radna mjesta
why_relevant: National employment bureau where Montenegrin employers, including banks and payment/IT firms, are legally expected to publish vacancy notices. Job titles and required skills (card systems, core banking, instant payments, AML tooling) are the cheapest leading indicator of technology and roadmap decisions.

source_name: Bankar.me — rubrika OGLASI ZA POSAO (banking job ads)
why_relevant: Montenegrin banking trade portal that republishes bank vacancy notices with full text. Acts as a single aggregated feed of hiring signals across CBCG, Prva banka, CKB, Komercijalna banka and others — far cheaper to monitor than each bank's own careers page.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka, OTP Group) — Posao u banci / careers
why_relevant: Largest ME bank by digital footprint; its own vacancy list reveals platform names, digital-channel teams and vendor-adjacent roles months before any disclosure. OTP Group ownership means group-level platform migrations surface here first.

The actual applicant-tracking board behind CKB hiring — structured, machine-readable vacancy objects with department and location, better for automated diffing than the CMS career page. Presence of an external ATS is itself a vendor signal.
